claim: systemd offers native failure-notification hooks: the [Unit] OnFailure= directive activates another unit when a unit fails, and the [Service] ExecStopPost= directive runs an arbitrary command after the service stops (including on failure) — e.g. ExecStopPost=/usr/bin/notify-send 'Service X failed!'.
stance_target: event-driven failed-unit notification needs no polling; a fleet agent can install OnFailure= drop-ins or ExecStopPost= hooks that push to MQTT instead of running systemctl --failed on a timer
scope_conditions: systemd units; ExecStopPost runs on any stop including failure; OnFailure= accepts unit names
quoted_support: There’s OnFailure (which lets you specify another service) and ExecStopPost (which lets you specify an arbitrary command). Something like this: [Unit] Description=My X service [Service] ExecStart=/usr/bin/false ExecStopPost=/usr/bin/notify-send "Service X failed!"

claim: 'systemctl status --failed' output embeds per-run timestamps and transient status text, so diffing consecutive outputs always reports a change even when the failed-unit set is identical; the stable form for change detection is 'systemctl --failed' (list only).
stance_target: if the agent polls failed units at all, it must use the stable list form (systemctl --failed) or parse JSON (--output=json) rather than diffing status output
quoted_support: a new problem was that it triggers every time, because when it runs systemctl status --failed it records the timestamp when it ran. So it was always different from the old. So I changed it to use the less chatty systemctl --failed instead.

claim: A community polling monitor for failed systemd units required multiple iterations to become reliable: guarding with 'grep failed' so fixed units don't re-alert from output drift, and icon-name portability issues (system-error vs computer-fail-symbolic vary by system).
stance_target: evidence that ad-hoc shell-based unit monitoring is fragile — motivating a properly engineered agent subsystem
scope_conditions: KDE Plasma desktop; Scriptinator plasmoid; sh scripts
quoted_support: if ! cmp --quiet systemd-status systemd-status.old then if grep failed systemd-status then ... else cp systemd-status systemd-status.old fi
